content:
Gray is more than a neutral color. It represents balance, calm, and quiet strength. In this post, you will find a wide range of gray shades, from soft light tones to deep charcoal hues. Each shade has its own look, mood, and purpose, even when the difference feels subtle.

This post covers both true achromatic grays, made only from black and white, and low-saturation gray tones with a hint of color. Pure grayscale shades include gainsboro and silver, while grayish colors such as taupe, ash, and cadet gray bring gentle warmth or coolness. You will see hex, RGB, and CMYK codes, along with meanings and common uses, to help you choose the right gray for design, art, or everyday projects.

Gray

Gray is the quintessential neutral, a perfect balance of black and white. This fundamental achromatic shade represents compromise and neutrality. Historically linked to industrial materials and modernist design, it conveys sophistication, calm, and formality. Consequently, it is a cornerstone in corporate branding, technology, and minimalist interiors for its timeless versatility.

  • HEX: #808080
  • RGB: 128, 128, 128
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 50

Light Gray

Light Gray is a very pale tone, evoking a sense of airiness and space. It is a near-white neutral that softens and brightens. This shade suggests cleanliness, simplicity, and modernity. Often used as a background, it is essential in UI design, contemporary architecture, and Scandinavian interiors to create an open, serene feel.

  • HEX: #D3D3D3
  • RGB: 211, 211, 211
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 17

Dark Gray

Dark Gray is a deep, muted tone leaning toward black but retaining complexity. It provides a strong, sober foundation for palettes. This color implies authority, resilience, and seriousness. As a result, it is frequently chosen for professional typography, luxury automotive finishes, and industrial design where understated strength is key.

  • HEX: #A9A9A9
  • RGB: 169, 169, 169
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 34

Charcoal

Charcoal is an extremely dark gray with subtle blue undertones, reminiscent of burnt wood. This deep, intense shade is associated with power and drama. It conveys sophistication, mystery, and solidity. Therefore, it is popular in fashion for formalwear, high-contrast graphic design, and modern kitchen cabinetry.

  • HEX: #36454F
  • RGB: 54, 69, 79
  • CMYK: 32, 13, 0, 69

Ash Gray

Ash Gray is a soft, greenish-gray reminiscent of wood ash. This cool, muted tone evokes a natural, weathered quality. It suggests calm, neutrality, and subtlety. Consequently, it is commonly found in home decor, woolen fabrics, and landscape painting to provide a quiet, organic backdrop.

  • HEX: #B2BEB5
  • RGB: 178, 190, 181
  • CMYK: 6, 0, 5, 25

Silver

Silver is a metallic gray that mimics the lustrous precious metal. It represents modernity, innovation, and wealth. This shade is linked to glamour, high-tech, and futurism. As a result, it is iconic in automotive design, jewelry, and awards iconography to signify a sleek, second-place prestige.

  • HEX: #C0C0C0
  • RGB: 192, 192, 192
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 25

Slate Gray

Slate Gray is a medium gray with distinct blue undertones, inspired by slate rock. This cool, stony hue implies reliability, endurance, and practicality. It carries a sense of natural strength and stability. Thus, it is effectively used in roofing materials, professional software interfaces, and tailored suits.

  • HEX: #708090
  • RGB: 112, 128, 144
  • CMYK: 22, 11, 0, 44

Light Slate Gray

Light Slate Gray is a lighter, airier version of its base color, retaining the blue cast. It offers a softer, more approachable feel than darker slate. This tone suggests clarity, calm, and openness. Often, it is employed in web design elements, coastal interior accents, and winter fashion for a crisp, cool effect.

  • HEX: #778899
  • RGB: 119, 136, 153
  • CMYK: 22, 11, 0, 40

Dark Slate Gray

Dark Slate Gray is a very deep, cool gray that borders on black. It is one of the darkest web grays with a green-blue depth. This color conveys profundity, tradition, and weight. Accordingly, it serves as a powerful, serious background in data visualization, formal documents, and deep-space imagery.

  • HEX: #2F4F4F
  • RGB: 47, 79, 79
  • CMYK: 41, 0, 0, 69

Smoke

Smoke is a medium gray with a slight brown or green inflection, mimicking wisps of smoke. This ambiguous, hazy shade evokes mystery, transition, and softness. It implies an ethereal and fleeting quality. Therefore, it is used in product packaging, atmospheric photography, and textile dyes for a muted, sophisticated touch.

  • HEX: #738276
  • RGB: 115, 130, 118
  • CMYK: 12, 0, 9, 49

Pewter

Pewter is a muted, blue-gray tone inspired by the traditional metal alloy of tin and lead. This historical, soft metallic shade carries an antique and subdued character. It suggests durability, tradition, and understated elegance. Consequently, it is frequently used in tableware, vintage decor, and traditional jewelry design for its timeless, muted sheen.

  • HEX: #8A8F8E
  • RGB: 138, 143, 142
  • CMYK: 3, 0, 1, 44

Steel Gray

Steel Gray is a solid, medium-cool gray that directly mimics industrial steel. This strong, functional hue represents resilience, efficiency, and modernity. It evokes industrial strength and engineered precision. As a result, it is foundational in manufacturing branding, appliance finishes, and architectural cladding.

  • HEX: #71797E
  • RGB: 113, 121, 126
  • CMYK: 10, 4, 0, 51

Cool Gray

Cool Gray is a gray with pronounced blue or violet undertones, sitting distinctly on the cool side of the spectrum. This calm, detached shade is perceived as professional, serene, and technological. It is often associated with intellect and futurism. Therefore, it is a staple in corporate logos, tech product design, and medical environments.

  • HEX: #8C92AC
  • RGB: 140, 146, 172
  • CMYK: 19, 15, 0, 33

Warm Gray

Warm Gray is a gray infused with subtle brown, yellow, or red undertones, giving it a cozy feel. This inviting, earthy neutral suggests comfort, approachability, and natural simplicity. It counteracts the sterility of pure gray. Thus, it is extensively used in living room interiors, pottery, and paper stocks to create a welcoming atmosphere.

  • HEX: #A89F91
  • RGB: 168, 159, 145
  • CMYK: 0, 5, 14, 34

Cement

Cement is a straightforward, mid-tone gray that mimics the look of dried concrete. This urban, utilitarian shade represents raw modernity, structure, and practicality. It carries an unfinished, industrial aesthetic. Accordingly, it is central to brutalist architecture, urban fashion, and minimalist product design.

  • HEX: #8A8D8F
  • RGB: 138, 141, 143
  • CMYK: 3, 1, 0, 44

Graphite

Graphite is a very dark gray with a slight glossy sheen, reminiscent of pencil lead or crystalline carbon. This deep, rich shade implies sophistication, conductivity, and density. It is associated with writing, engineering, and luxury. Hence, it is favored for premium electronics, sleek automotive paint, and professional art supplies.

  • HEX: #474A51
  • RGB: 71, 74, 81
  • CMYK: 12, 9, 0, 68

Gunmetal

Gunmetal is an extremely dark gray with blue-green undertones, resembling blued steel. This somber, powerful color evokes strength, authority, and military precision. It suggests durability and formidable technology. Often, it is used for hardware tools, tactical gear, and high-end watch finishes.

  • HEX: #2A3439
  • RGB: 42, 52, 57
  • CMYK: 26, 9, 0, 78

Iron

Iron is a dark, neutral gray that captures the color of cast or wrought iron. This heavy, foundational shade represents sturdiness, tradition, and raw power. It has a no-nonsense, elemental quality. Consequently, it appears in historic machinery, wrought iron gates, and industrial-inspired furniture.

  • HEX: #4C4F56
  • RGB: 76, 79, 86
  • CMYK: 12, 8, 0, 66

Lead

Lead is a dull, medium-dark gray inspired by the heavy metal. This dense, muted tone historically signifies weight and toxicity, but also permanence. It carries a subdued and serious mood. Thus, it is used in radiation shielding symbolism, somber artistic works, and vintage print typography.

  • HEX: #575B5D
  • RGB: 87, 91, 93
  • CMYK: 6, 2, 0, 64

Stone Gray

Stone Gray is a gray with clear beige or taupe undertones, mimicking natural river rock. This organic, weathered shade suggests stability, natural elegance, and timelessness. It connects to earth and ancient structures. Therefore, it is ideal for exterior facades, landscape design, and rustic ceramic glazes.

  • HEX: #928E85
  • RGB: 146, 142, 133
  • CMYK: 0, 3, 9, 43

Cloud Gray

Cloud Gray is a very light, soft gray that evokes the diffuse underside of a cloud. This ethereal and gentle shade suggests softness, tranquility, and openness. It is inherently calming and expansive. Consequently, it is a popular choice for bedroom ceilings, spa interiors, and soft-focus photography backdrops to create a serene, airy mood.

  • HEX: #B7B7B7
  • RGB: 183, 183, 183
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 28

Dove Gray

Dove Gray is a soft, warm gray with hints of brown or lavender, inspired by the bird’s plumage. This gentle, peaceful hue symbolizes peace, gentility, and subtle luxury. It carries a quietly sophisticated tone. Thus, it is frequently used in wedding stationery, high-end linens, and classic tailored fashion.

  • HEX: #6D6C6C
  • RGB: 109, 108, 108
  • CMYK: 0, 1, 1, 57

Flint

Flint is a hard, dark gray with cool undertones, resembling the sedimentary rock used for tools. This sharp, resilient shade implies durability, spark, and primordial utility. It evokes a sense of striking potential. Therefore, it is applied in outdoor gear, modern sculptural materials, and rugged tech accessories.

  • HEX: #7E7D79
  • RGB: 126, 125, 121
  • CMYK: 0, 1, 4, 51

Fossil

Fossil is a muted, grayish-taupe that mimics ancient, preserved remains in stone. This ancient, subtle color suggests history, endurance, and natural discovery. It carries a quiet, archaeological intrigue. Accordingly, it is chosen for museum displays, heritage branding, and earth-toned pottery.

  • HEX: #787276
  • RGB: 120, 114, 118
  • CMYK: 0, 5, 2, 53

Nickel

Nickel is a medium-light gray with a slight reflective quality, named for the silvery-white metal. This cool, modern metallic hue represents hygiene, resilience, and industrial alloy. It suggests a smooth, clean surface. Hence, it is common in appliance finishes, commercial hardware, and contemporary jewelry settings.

  • HEX: #727472
  • RGB: 114, 116, 114
  • CMYK: 2, 0, 2, 55

Platinum

Platinum is a very light, slightly warm gray that imitates the precious metal, brighter than silver. This rare, prestigious shade denotes luxury, value, and cool elegance. It is associated with enduring quality and milestone achievements. As a result, it is iconic for award trophies, wedding bands, and premium automotive trim.

  • HEX: #E5E4E2
  • RGB: 229, 228, 226
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 1, 10

Mercury

Mercury is a soft, fluid gray named for the liquid metal, also known as Quicksilver. This elusive, shimmering shade evokes motion, fluidity, and scientific intrigue. It suggests speed and transformation. Thus, it is used in sports car accents, tech logos symbolizing speed, and mystical or alchemical art.

  • HEX: #BEBEBE
  • RGB: 190, 190, 190
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 25

Alloy

Alloy is a grayish-taupe that represents the blended, non-specific color of mixed metals. This composite, industrial shade implies innovation, strength through combination, and engineered material. It lacks a single metallic identity. Consequently, it appears in industrial design, stealth product finishes, and futuristic concept art.

  • HEX: #98979A
  • RGB: 152, 151, 154
  • CMYK: 1, 2, 0, 40

Battleship Gray

Battleship Gray is a medium, slightly greenish-gray historically used for naval camouflage. This functional, no-nonsense color represents utility, authority, and maritime durability. It is designed to be unobtrusive and tough. Therefore, it remains popular for military equipment, workshop tools, and heavy-duty outdoor furniture.

  • HEX: #848482
  • RGB: 132, 132, 130
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 2, 48

Shadow

Shadow is a deep, neutral gray that mimics the darkest part of a cast shadow. This ubiquitous, dimensional shade represents depth, mystery, and subtle contrast. It is essential for creating visual volume. As such, it is fundamental in photography, painting for shading, and UI design for drop shadows.

  • HEX: #5A5A5A
  • RGB: 90, 90, 90
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 65

Smoke Gray

Smoke Gray is a medium, muted gray with a slightly brownish or greenish cast, reminiscent of dissipating smoke. This ambiguous and hazy shade evokes a sense of mystery and soft transition. The color suggests an ethereal and fleeting quality, making it feel sophisticated and subtle. Therefore, Smoke Gray is effectively used in product packaging, atmospheric photography, and textile dyes to add a muted, elegant touch.

  • HEX: #7D7F7D
  • RGB: 125, 127, 125
  • CMYK: 2, 0, 2, 50

Granite

Granite is a speckled medium-dark gray inspired by the igneous rock. This speckled, textured shade implies permanence, durability, and natural strength. Granite carries an unshakeable and elegant connotation due to its use as a building material. Consequently, it is a prime choice for countertops, monumental architecture, and rugged outdoor apparel to communicate solidity and timelessness.

  • HEX: #676767
  • RGB: 103, 103, 103
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 60

Concrete

Concrete is a cool, light to medium gray that directly mimics poured and cured urban concrete. This urban, utilitarian shade represents raw modernity, structure, and practicality. The color carries an unfinished, industrial aesthetic that is both stark and versatile. Accordingly, Concrete is central to brutalist architecture, urban fashion, and minimalist product design where a raw, honest materiality is desired.

  • HEX: #95A0A3
  • RGB: 149, 160, 163
  • CMYK: 9, 2, 0, 36

Pearl Gray

Pearl Gray is a very light gray with a warm, iridescent quality, like a natural pearl. This lustrous, delicate shade suggests luxury, purity, and subtle glamour. Pearl Gray evokes softness and refined elegance, unlike brighter metallic shades. Thus, it is favored for bridal fashion, luxury cosmetics packaging, and high-end interior trim to impart a soft, luminous glow.

  • HEX: #E2DFD2
  • RGB: 226, 223, 210
  • CMYK: 0, 1, 7, 11

Tin

Tin is a dull, cool medium gray that reflects the color of the untreated metal. This muted, industrial hue implies modest utility, malleability, and a vintage industrial feel. Tin lacks the prestige of silver but carries historical authenticity. Hence, it is used in vintage toy replicas, steampunk aesthetics, and historical restoration projects.

  • HEX: #919191
  • RGB: 145, 145, 145
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 43

Lunar Gray

Lunar Gray is a very light, cool gray that captures the ashen color of the moon’s surface. This desolate, serene shade evokes mystery, space, and cool reflection. Lunar Gray suggests calm isolation and futuristic exploration. As a result, it is popular in sci-fi themed design, modern electronics, and minimalist spaceships to create an otherworldly atmosphere.

  • HEX: #BFC0C0
  • RGB: 191, 192, 192
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 25

Mist Gray

Mist Gray is a light, cool gray with a blue undertone, like a mountain mist. This cool, ephemeral shade suggests obscurity, softness, and a fresh chill. Mist Gray creates a light, airy, and somewhat mysterious mood. Therefore, it is ideal for cosmetic branding, serene landscape art, and website backgrounds aiming for a clean, ethereal feel.

  • HEX: #C4C4C4
  • RGB: 196, 196, 196
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 23

Frost Gray

Frost Gray is a very light gray with a strong blue undertone, mimicking frost on a windowpane. This crisp, icy shade conveys cold, clarity, and a pristine freshness. Frost Gray implies a sparkling, tranquil winter feeling. Consequently, it is used in winter holiday designs, skincare product packaging, and cool-themed UI elements.

  • HEX: #D8D8D8
  • RGB: 216, 216, 216
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 15

Storm Gray

Storm Gray is a deep, cool gray with blue undertones, reminiscent of heavy storm clouds. This powerful, ominous hue represents impending change, dramatic tension, and natural power. Storm Gray carries a sobering and intense energy. Thus, it is effective for dramatic photography backdrops, thriller movie posters, and performance outerwear.

  • HEX: #747880
  • RGB: 116, 120, 128
  • CMYK: 9, 6, 0, 50

Rain Gray

Rain Gray is a medium, cool gray that captures the color of a rainy sky or wet pavement. This damp, reflective shade evokes melancholy, renewal, and urban sleekness. The color suggests a clean, subdued, and reflective mood after a downpour. Accordingly, Rain Gray is chosen for rainwear, modern urban architecture, and contemplative literary book covers.

  • HEX: #9DA3A6
  • RGB: 157, 163, 166
  • CMYK: 5, 2, 0, 35

Fog

Fog is a light, warm gray that mimics the visual effect of thick atmospheric fog. This obscuring, softening shade represents ambiguity, mystery, and a blurring of boundaries. Fog creates a dreamlike and muted atmosphere, reducing contrast and sharpness. Therefore, this color is ideal for backgrounds in art to imply distance, in fashion for soft layers, and in interior design to create a cozy, enclosed feel.

  • HEX: #AEAEAE
  • RGB: 174, 174, 174
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 32

Marble Gray

Marble Gray is a light to medium gray with subtle, streaked variations, inspired by natural stone. This veined, luxurious shade implies classical elegance, cool sophistication, and timeless artistry. Marble Gray carries a stately and high-end connotation from centuries of architectural use. Consequently, it is ubiquitous in luxury hotel lobbies, high-end cosmetics packaging, and classical sculpture replicas.

  • HEX: #C6C6C6
  • RGB: 198, 198, 198
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 22

Ironstone

Ironstone is a deep, solid gray with a slight brown undertone, named for the dense pottery and rock. This heavy, opaque color suggests durability, rustic strength, and historical craft. Ironstone has a substantial and earthy quality, different from cooler industrial grays. Thus, it is used in traditional stoneware, heritage brand logos, and rugged outdoor furniture finishes.

  • HEX: #555555
  • RGB: 85, 85, 85
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 67

Gravel

Gravel is a medium-dark, desaturated gray-brown that mimics crushed stone. This textured, utilitarian shade represents functionality, pathways, and granular texture. Gravel implies a rough, practical, and unrefined nature. As a result, it is applied in landscaping themes, workwear fabrics, and automotive undercoatings to communicate toughness and grit.

  • HEX: #6B6E70
  • RGB: 107, 110, 112
  • CMYK: 4, 2, 0, 56

Thunder Gray

Thunder Gray is a very dark, neutral gray that evokes the sky before a thunderclap. This ominous, charged shade conveys power, impending drama, and deep resonance. Thunder Gray carries a heavy and atmospheric weight. Hence, it is powerful for sound equipment branding, dramatic stage lighting filters, and luxury men’s fragrance packaging.

  • HEX: #4F4F4F
  • RGB: 79, 79, 79
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 69

Moon Dust

Moon Dust is a very light, slightly warm gray with a powdery texture association. This soft, cosmic shade suggests delicacy, mystery, and extraterrestrial landscape. Moon Dust evokes a sense of fine, loose particles and serene exploration. Accordingly, it is used in space-themed graphics, ethereal wedding palettes, and high-tech fabric names.

  • HEX: #B4B4B4
  • RGB: 180, 180, 180
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 29

Urban Gray

Urban Gray is a versatile mid-tone gray that captures the color of city concrete and asphalt from a distance. This modern, ubiquitous shade represents metropolitan life, anonymity, and structural grid. Urban Gray is the essential color of the built environment. Therefore, it is foundational in streetwear, contemporary product design, and architectural renderings.

  • HEX: #9E9E9E
  • RGB: 158, 158, 158
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 38

Neutral Gray

Neutral Gray is a pure, balanced gray with no discernible warm or cool undertones. This perfectly achromatic shade is the baseline for color calibration and true neutrality. Neutral Gray represents impartiality, balance, and technical reference. Consequently, it is critical in photography gray cards, scientific equipment, and UI design systems as an unbiased background.

  • HEX: #8E8E8E
  • RGB: 142, 142, 142
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 44

Carbon

Carbon is an extremely dark gray, nearly black, inspired by elemental carbon. This deep, rich shade signifies essential building blocks, strength, and high-tech materiality. Carbon is associated with both primal soot and advanced composites. As a result, it is used in sports car components (carbon fiber), sleek audio equipment, and minimalist typography.

  • HEX: #2E2E2E
  • RGB: 46, 46, 46
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 82

Jet Gray

Jet Gray is a deep, solid gray with a name derived from the compact black gemstone. This intense, polished shade conveys sophistication, severity, and a sleek modernity. Jet Gray sits on the border between black and gray, offering slightly more nuance than pure black. Therefore, it is favored for luxury watch faces, formal evening wear, and high-end electronics where a deep, refined darkness is required.

  • HEX: #3A3A3A
  • RGB: 58, 58, 58
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 77

Frosted Silver

Frosted Silver is a very light gray with a diffuse, matte finish that suggests a frosted glass or metal surface. This soft, muted metallic hue implies modern elegance, diffused light, and subtle coolness. Unlike shiny silver, Frosted Silver has a gentle and contemporary feel. Consequently, it is popular for appliance finishes, modern jewelry, and UI elements where a soft glow is desired.

  • HEX: #DDDDDD
  • RGB: 221, 221, 221
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 13

Antique Gray

Antique Gray is a medium gray with warm, brown undertones that suggest aged wood or weathered stone. This historic, timeworn shade evokes nostalgia, authenticity, and crafted heritage. Antique Gray carries a patina of age and story. Thus, it is extensively used in restored furniture, vintage-inspired packaging, and historical film set design to create an aged, authentic look.

  • HEX: #8F8F8F
  • RGB: 143, 143, 143
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 44

Industrial Gray

Industrial Gray is a straightforward, mid-tone cool gray synonymous with factory floors and machinery. This functional, no-frills color represents efficiency, mass production, and rugged utility. Industrial Gray is the archetypal color of the working machine. As a result, it is a staple for toolboxes, warehouse interiors, and industrial design prototypes.

  • HEX: #7A7A7A
  • RGB: 122, 122, 122
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 52

Platinum Gray

Platinum Gray is a light, cool gray that mimics the precious metal but with a softer, less reflective quality. This prestige, contemporary shade suggests exclusive modernity, cool wealth, and sleek innovation. Platinum Gray is lighter and softer than charcoal, but more serious than silver. Hence, it is used in luxury automotive interiors, high-tech gadgetry, and premium cosmetic packaging.

  • HEX: #DADADA
  • RGB: 218, 218, 218
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 15

Lunar Rock

Lunar Rock is a muted, greenish-gray that captures the color of moon rock samples and space-age materials. This futuristic, dusty shade implies exploration, advanced tech, and a muted otherworldliness. Lunar Rock feels both natural and synthetic. Accordingly, it has become trendy in activewear, crossover vehicle paints, and modern kitchen appliances.

  • HEX: #B0B1AF
  • RGB: 176, 177, 175
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 1, 31

Arctic Gray

Arctic Gray is an extremely light, cool gray with blue undertones, evoking ice fields and frozen skies. This crisp, serene shade conveys purity, isolation, and frigid calm. Arctic Gray is the color of vast, open cold. Therefore, it is effective for winter sportswear branding, refrigerators, and designs aiming for a stark, clean, and expansive aesthetic.

  • HEX: #E1E1E1
  • RGB: 225, 225, 225
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 12

Cosmic Gray

Cosmic Gray is a medium, slightly desaturated gray with a hint of blue, suggesting the void of space dotted with distant matter. This mysterious, expansive shade represents the infinite, the unknown, and deep mystery. Cosmic Gray feels both empty and full of potential. Consequently, it is used in astronomy software interfaces, sci-fi book covers, and deep-tech company branding.

  • HEX: #9B9EA1
  • RGB: 155, 158, 161
  • CMYK: 4, 2, 0, 37

Mystic Gray

Mystic Gray is a medium, neutral gray with a name that implies hidden depths and ambiguity. This enigmatic, balanced shade suggests mystery, intuition, and a bridge between worlds. Mystic Gray is neither warm nor cool, inviting interpretation. Thus, it appears in spiritual and wellness branding, magic-themed games, and abstract art.

  • HEX: #A0A0A0
  • RGB: 160, 160, 160
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 37

Skyline Gray

Skyline Gray is a light, grayish-beige or gray-green that mimics the hazy color of distant city silhouettes against the sky. This atmospheric, urban shade evokes distance, pollution haze, and the blend of nature and city. Skyline Gray has a soft, blurred, and complex quality. As a result, it is chosen for architectural models, travel blog aesthetics, and sophisticated menswear.

  • HEX: #B5B8B1
  • RGB: 181, 184, 177
  • CMYK: 2, 0, 4, 28

Chalk Gray

Chalk Gray is a very light, slightly warm gray with a matte, dusty texture reminiscent of a chalkboard or pastel. This dry, soft shade suggests education, simplicity, and temporary marking. Chalk Gray evokes a tactile, nostalgic feel of classrooms and hand-drawn sketches. Therefore, it is used in craft packaging, educational materials for children, and rustic wedding decor to create an approachable, artisanal mood.

  • HEX: #D6D6D6
  • RGB: 214, 214, 214
  • CMYK: 0, 0, 0, 16

Quartz Gray

Quartz Gray is a clean, light to medium gray inspired by the engineered stone and natural mineral. This smooth, consistent shade implies modernity, engineered perfection, and cool clarity. Quartz Gray carries a sanitary and sleek connotation from its use in countertops. Consequently, it is popular for kitchen and bathroom design, laboratory surfaces, and tech product housings.

  • HEX: #A5A5A5
  • RGB: 165, 165, 165
